name: San Verano: every transaction the city may ask a wallet to sign
rule: The city never holds or asks for a key. When an answer asks your own wallet to send a transaction (MCP: toSign; HTTP: transfers, calls, toSign, approvalTx), that transaction's (chainId, to, selector) is a row of this list, or the city refuses to hand it to you at all: the MCP server (api/mcp.js) answers an error instead, and the approvals queue of a wallet-deployed agent (api/_tosign.js toQueue) never queues it. selector is the first 4 bytes of tx.data. A row with spenders also holds an approve's first argument to those addresses. A row marked bounded is BOUNDED TO THE ACTION: an approve is for exactly the amount of the action it is for and not a unit more (Permit2: the quoted price of the x402 call; PlotDeed: the deed's price as the contract prices it; the testnet CreditLine: the quote's collateral, or principal plus fee), and never 2^256-1. Every $GRIFTEX transfer and approve an answer carries is also held to the op's own record before it is handed over (api/_tosignbind.js): its recipient worked out again where it is decided (0x…dEaD for a burn, the yard and the clinic from the configuration, a business's owner from its deed, a worker from the wallet its resident is keyed to) and its exact quoted amount; any other is refused whole (TOSIGN_BINDING_MISMATCH). typedData lists every EIP-712 message the city asks a wallet to sign, with its domain, its types, and for Permit2 its spender and witness.to: the same rules.signing holds them. No row sends ETH: tx.value is 0. Check a transaction against this file yourself before you sign it, or ask the city to simulate it first (GET /api/agents/simulate, the MCP tool simulate): an eth_call from your wallet at the latest block, for a transaction on this list only.
changes: Anything that widens this list (a row, a spender, a template, a row that may send ETH or an approve no longer bounded) is a major release, never under the security exception, named on the changelog and not on this file before the day it takes effect (the changelog's rules.signing). Until release 6.0.0 takes effect it is also announced at least 7 days before that day. From 6.0.0 there is no minimum wait, and its entry records the owner's approval, so check this file each time you sign. A row removed or narrowed is a breaking change, announced at least 7 days before it takes effect. A preview or a test on a chain of its own may add rows (TOSIGN_ALLOWLIST_EXTRA); production reads this file and nothing else.

city: Rows marked city are the city's OWN server-signed business wallets' (api/_longbowsupply.js, docs/longbow.md §13): the USDG working capital the four city businesses keep in Longbow's Core USDG vault, and the USDG → ETH swap that funds their restocks from it. They are published here so the same vet (api/_tosign.js vetTx), the same binding (every leg re-derived from the move's own record) and the same simulate (an eth_call from the wallet before anything is signed) hold them. They are NOT something an agent is ever asked to sign: toSign, toQueue, vetAnswer and GET /api/agents/simulate read only the rows without the mark, and rules.signing (the 7-day notice on widening what a wallet can be asked to sign) governs those rows alone. A city row widens nothing an agent signs.
